priority: P2 — gap inventory G6. A0-U6 is the last EMPTY A0 unit: the map teaches ser + adjectives, family review, weather and simple questions. No shipped pack carries a single weather word, a single descriptor beyond grande/pequeña/bonita, or a single question word. exam-a0 tests none of these, so nothing is exam-blocked — this is a content prerequisite, same class as G3.
why: Weather already leaks into shipped text unbound: a0-u02 speaks «hace frío» (enero, febrero, noviembre), «hace calor» (julio), «hace sol» (junio), «hay viento» (marzo, octubre), «llueve» (abril, septiembre) and «hay nieve» (diciembre) with no pool id behind any of them — DEFECTS #14 in reverse (a heard word replay cannot serve). U6 makes all six real ids and binds the pattern that asks about them. It also closes the descriptor holes in shipped captions: a0-signs says «la cueva es oscura», a0-u04 says «el plato está limpio», a0-u05 says «el sur es caliente» and «el desierto es seco» — none of those adjectives is an id. Question words are the last A0 gap before A1-U1 revisits them in depth.
theme: El tiempo y cómo son las cosas — weather, describing things, and simple questions
storyThread: Rut y Noemí en el camino (Rut 1–2): el tiempo, el campo y la casa

words.say: ¿Cómo está el tiempo? Mira el cielo.
words.caption: ¿Cómo está el tiempo?
words.note: the question that opens every weather talk; answer with hace frío, hace sol or está nublado

words.caption: Hace frío
words.note: weather uses hacer: hace frío = it is cold. frío alone is the adjective (wave 2)

words.caption: Hace calor
words.note: hace calor = it is hot; the opposite of hace frío

words.say: Hoy hace sol en el pueblo.
words.caption: Hace sol
words.note: hace sol = the sun is out. sol alone (a0-verbs) is the sun itself

words.caption: Hace viento
words.note: viento = wind; hace viento = it is windy

words.caption: Llueve
words.note: from llover; one word says it all. ll sounds like the y in yes

words.caption: La nieve blanca
words.note: nieve = snow (noun): hay nieve = there is snow. a0-u02 already says hay nieve en diciembre

words.caption: El cielo nublado
words.note: nublado = cloudy; this weather takes está, not hace: el cielo está nublado

words.caption: El viento frío
words.note: frío / fría: el viento frío, el agua fría. hace frío is the weather; frío describes a thing

words.caption: El pan caliente
words.note: caliente is the same for masculine and feminine: el pan caliente, el agua caliente

words.caption: Un pan nuevo
words.note: nuevo / nueva: un pan nuevo, una cesta nueva. un pan nuevo = fresh bread

words.caption: El árbol viejo
words.note: viejo / vieja: el árbol viejo, la casa vieja. for things, not people

words.caption: El camino limpio
words.note: limpio / limpia: el camino limpio, la casa limpia

words.caption: El saco sucio
words.note: sucio / sucia: el saco sucio, las manos sucias

words.caption: El bosque oscuro
words.note: oscuro / oscura: el bosque oscuro, la cueva oscura

words.caption: El barro mojado
words.note: mojado / mojada: mojado = wet. after llueve the camino is mojado

words.caption: El camino seco
words.note: seco / seca: the opposite of mojado

words.caption: Frío en invierno
words.note: invierno = winter; en invierno = in winter

words.caption: Calor en verano
words.note: verano = summer; en verano = in summer

words.caption: Viento en otoño
words.note: otoño = autumn; ñ sounds like the ny in canyon

words.say: En primavera el campo es verde.
words.caption: El campo verde
words.note: primavera = spring; el campo es verde = the countryside is green

words.say: Noemí mira el tiempo de hoy.
words.caption: El tiempo de hoy
words.note: tiempo = weather (and time): el tiempo de hoy = today's weather. hora is the hour, fecha is the date

words.caption: ¿Qué es esto?
words.note: qué = what; the accent marks the question word (que without an accent = that)

words.caption: ¿Cómo estás?
words.note: cómo = how; unit-01 already said ¿Cómo te llamas? — same word. cómo (how) and como (I eat, a0-verbs) differ only by the accent

words.caption: ¿Dónde está mi casa?
words.note: dónde = where; dónde asks a place, quién asks a person

words.caption: ¿Quién es?
words.note: quién = who; one syllable: KYEN

words.caption: ¿Cuándo vamos?
words.note: cuándo = when; cuando without an accent is not a question

words.caption: ¿Cuál es tu casa?
words.note: cuál = which; a0-u02 already says ¿Cuál es la fecha hoy?

WAVE_NOTE: Wave map: 1 = weather (the pattern ¿Cómo está el tiempo? is the anchor tile, then the five hace-phrases, llueve, nieve, nublado — hear-choose, no sprites required); 2 = ser/estar + adjective (the grammar heart: 9 descriptors, each tile is the citation form and the note carries the -a agreement); 3 = seasons + tiempo (pairs with a0-u02's twelve months); 4 = the question wave (6 interrogatives as plain tiles, no sprites). NEAR-PAIR SEPARATION is deliberate: hace frío (w1) vs frío (w2), hace sol (w1) vs sol (a0-verbs), ¿Cómo está el tiempo? (w1) vs cómo (w4), tiempo (w3) vs hora/fecha (a0-u02) — no two members of a near pair share a wave, and no option set contains both members. Largest wave is 9 — no pagination needed (DEFECTS #18 threshold is 12). LEAD RULE 19:59: waves 1-4 + replay-5 as delivered.

QA.charset: ASCII + á é í ó ú ñ ¿ ¡ only in rendered fields; no « » anywhere in this pack
QA.grammar: present tense only (es, está, hay, hace, llueve, tengo, vamos, mira-imperative); no past, no subjunctive. ser/estar rule documented per word: es for what something is like, está for how it is now. Both copulas are already bound ids (es = unit-01, está = a0-verbs)
QA.countDecision: 28 = 8 weather + 9 descriptors + 5 season/time + 6 question words. Descriptors overshoot the brief's 6-8 by one (sucio kept — limpio/sucio is the highest-value A0 pair) and question words by one (cuál added — a0-u02 already speaks it unbound). Total inside 25-30.
QA.weatherIdDecision: hace frío/calor/sol/viento are ids as PHRASES, not hace+frío+calor+sol+viento as five ids: (1) the learner hears the phrase as one unit (formIdRule); (2) sol/frío/calor would each need their own id and appear as bare tiles whose meaning is not the weather — five ids buys four phantom contrasts; (3) audio-first: an A0 learner cannot be told 'add hacer to sol'. Cost: 'hace' never a bound id alone — accepted (hacer ships in a0-verbs; the phrases carry the form)
QA.nieveDecision: nieve as the NOUN (snow), not the verb nieva: a0-u02 ships the noun use; the verb would be a third weather verb A0 does not need; nieve pairs with hielo (a0-u05) as a touchable thing
QA.descriptorDecision: Headword = masculine singular -o form (frío, nuevo, viejo, limpio, sucio, oscuro, mojado, seco) plus the invariant caliente. Pool already carries feminine forms (pequeña, bonita) and a masculine one (blanco) — teaching -o gives BOTH genders, each note states the -a switch
QA.questionWordDecision: Six: qué, cómo, dónde, quién, cuándo, cuál — bare accented forms, no ¿...? (the accent alone marks the interrogative; a bare word keeps the tile a WORD and avoids a second id space). The pattern ¿Cómo está el tiempo? keeps its ¿...? because it is a phrase. EXCLUDED: por qué/para qué (A1-U1 owns question words in depth; por qué needs porque), cuántos (spoken unbound in a0-u02 but belongs to the numbers follow-up; cuántos/cuándo is an A0 listening trap — flagged, not closed)
QA.seasonDecision: Seasons in U6, not U2: the bridge from a0-u02's months to weather (en enero hace frío / en invierno hace frío); no pack carries them. tiempo included because the pattern id contains it and every weather line needs the noun, with hora/fecha as bound decoys making the weather-vs-clock sense explicit
QA.duplicateCheck: Zero overlap with unit-01 (53 distinct es incl. te llamas), a0-packs (49), a0-verbs (30), a0-u02 (45) — 28 new ids. Union after U6 = 205 (measured, LEAD 20:27: the 176-vs-177 discrepancy was unit-01's 53rd id 'te llamas' — settled)
QA.noReAdds: Deliberately NOT re-taught, only referenced in say/caption or as bound decoys: sol, grande, pequeña, bonita, es, está, tengo, vamos, hacer; hoy, hora, fecha, enero-diciembre; cielo, madre, tú; casa, saco, pan, agua, plato; campo, camino, árbol, barro, hielo, norte, sur; bosque, desierto, cueva; verde, blanco/blanca. No family word re-taught (all in unit-01) — family review is a lesson-layer task
QA.optionsBoundToIds: Every option string is a bound id in the union — no phantom decoys (DEFECTS #14). Decoy rule: within-wave semantic opposite (hace frío/hace calor, mojado/seco, limpio/sucio, nuevo/viejo) or within-wave neighbour, never a cross-wave near pair
QA.formIdRule: ids are the exact form the learner hears and the string on the tile: weather = phrase ids + single verbs + nouns + adjective (nublado); descriptors = masculine citation form (caliente invariant); seasons/time = nouns; questions = bare accented forms; the pattern keeps its ¿...?
QA.accentTrap: RENDERER/QA FLAG: this pack puts cómo into the pool beside a0-verbs' como — two bound ids differing only by an accent. If tiles don't render accents distinctly at game size, hear-choose items become unanswerable.
